solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cat and a bird endlessly going round tree

indicators.note: going round means the whole string of cat, a and trimmed bird is turned to read backwards

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

indicators.note: endlessly means the bird's name loses its final letter

parts.note: the grebe is a diving water bird

explanation.surface: A cat and a bird chasing each other round and round a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' leaves GREB, and 'going round' turns the whole run backwards; 'tree' sits at the end as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The bergamot is a small citrus tree whose fruit flavours Earl Grey tea.

clue.text: One tested bomb aboard chopper heading north east

indicators.note: in a down clue heading north means the chopper word reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: an axe is a chopper
a mine is a kind of bomb

explanation.surface: Someone tested by a bomb on board a helicopter flying north-east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopper' looks like a helicopter; it is an axe. 'heading north' turns AXE into EXA.
explanation.definitionFit: An examinee is a person sitting an exam.

clue.text: Bloke with pistol has terrorised treatment centre

parts.note: guy means bloke

indicators.note: terrorised suggests the letters of pistol has are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A man with a gun has terrorised a clinic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrorised' rearranges PISTOL HAS. Guy's Hospital is a teaching hospital in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital is a place where patients receive medical treatment.

clue.text: Spies on family to obtain material

parts.note: moles are spies planted in an organisation
kin means family

explanation.surface: Spies keeping watch on a family to get information.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' reads as intelligence; it is fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Moleskin is a heavy cotton fabric with a soft nap.

clue.text: Hear about ancient format Sophocles deployed

indicators.note: about means the word for hear goes round the word for ancient

parts.note: to try a case is to hear it in court
aged means ancient

explanation.surface: Listening to the old dramatic form that Sophocles used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear' is the legal sense: a judge hears, or tries, a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophocles wrote Greek tragedies such as Oedipus Rex.

clue.text: Artist in break spent fighting?

parts.note: war is fighting
hol is short for holiday, a break

explanation.surface: An artist who spent his holiday at war.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads as a 'war hol', a break spent fighting; HOL is British slang for holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Andy Warhol was the American pop artist.

clue.text: Company unlikely to collapse

explanation.definitionFit: Firm is both a noun for a business and an adjective for something solid.

clue.text: Criminal taking in brother in Tuscan city

indicators.note: taking in means the criminal holds the exclamation inside

parts.note: a fence is a criminal who handles stolen goods
'Brother!' and 'Lor!' (from Lord) are both exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: A criminal smuggling his brother into an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brother' is not a sibling but the exclamation, as in 'Oh brother!', equal to the old 'Lor!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Florence is the capital of Tuscany in Italy.

clue.text: In dark, wounded badly, duck remains flattened

indicators.note: In at the front says the duck sits inside the shuffled dark
wounded suggests the word dark is damaged and its letters knocked about

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nought, so O
badly can mean ill, as in 'ill-advised'

explanation.surface: Something badly hurt in the dark, perhaps a duck run over on a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wounded' gives RADK, which 'In' opens to take O. 'duck' looks like the bird; it is cricket's score of nought.
explanation.definitionFit: Roadkill is the flattened remains of animals hit by traffic.

clue.text: Sheep knocked over Yankee woman held in reverence

indicators.note: knocked over means the sheep word is upended and read backwards

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An American bowled over by a sheep, oddly reverent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' turns RAM into MAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary, mother of Jesus, is venerated in Christian worship.

clue.text: Ridiculous means by which Brazil may be entered?

definitions.text: Ridiculous means by which Brazil may be entered?

parts.words: Ridiculous means by which Brazil may be entered?
parts.note: Brazil is the Brazil nut, and taking a huge hammer to crack a nut is the stock image of absurd overkill

explanation.surface: A question about some absurd way of gaining entry to the country of Brazil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brazil' reads as the country; it is the nut, and 'entered' means broken into.
explanation.definitionFit: Using a heavy maul to crack a nut is the proverbial example of excessive force.

clue.text: One to keep order at sea, mum seconds calls to arrest a sailor

definitions.text: One to keep order at sea

parts.note: ma is a word for mum

indicators.note: to arrest means the calls word holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: terms are names, what things are called
tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: Mum quickly shouts for someone to arrest a sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'calls' is a noun here, the names things are called, and 'to arrest' means holding the sailor inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: A master-at-arms is a ship's officer responsible for discipline and policing.

clue.text: Free one for the French rugby player

parts.note: un is French for one
a lock is a second-row forward in rugby

explanation.surface: One free ticket for a French rugby player.
explanation.definitionFit: To unlock something is to release or set it free, a verb sense.

clue.text: Chap drinking beer, seldom "discontented" northerner

indicators.note: drinking means the chap takes the beer and the rest inside himself

parts.note: Dan is a man's name, standing for any chap
ale is a kind of beer

indicators.note: discontented means seldom has its contents removed, keeping only the outside letters

explanation.surface: A man rarely content, drinking his beer: a grumpy northern stereotype.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discontented' leaves SM, and the quotation marks flag that the word is being emptied, not that the man is unhappy.
explanation.definitionFit: A dalesman is a native of the Yorkshire Dales, valleys in northern England.

clue.text: Democrat given answer not right to lose heart

indicators.note: not means the right letter is to be left out of the word for answer

parts.note: to respond is to answer

explanation.surface: A Democrat given no correct answer starts to lose heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not right' drops R from RESPOND, leaving ESPOND.
explanation.definitionFit: To despond, an old verb, is to become dejected and give up hope.

clue.text: Stress less, taking drink before performance

indicators.note: before puts the drink ahead of the performance

parts.note: to down a drink is to drink it
a play is a theatrical performance

explanation.surface: Easing tension by having a drink before the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stress less' looks like advice to relax; it means to put less emphasis on.
explanation.definitionFit: To downplay something is to minimise its importance.

clue.text: Climate warmed with this shelter plunged into river?

indicators.note: plunged into means the shelter goes inside the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
a tent is a shelter

explanation.surface: A tent dunked in a river during unusually warm weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climate' is the political climate between nations, not the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Détente is an easing of hostility between nations, a thaw in relations.

clue.text: Poetic device exemplified in Keats and Yeats?

definitions.text: Poetic device exemplified in Keats and Yeats?

parts.words: Poetic device exemplified in Keats and Yeats?
parts.note: the two poets' names end in the same letters yet are said differently, so they match only on the page

explanation.surface: A literary question about a technique the two poets used.
explanation.walkthrough: It is the poets' names themselves, not their verse, that show the device.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye rhyme pairs words spelt alike but pronounced differently, like love and move.

clue.text: Tramp circling rocky ridge finds amphibian

indicators.note: circling means the tramp word goes round the ridge word

parts.note: to trog is to trudge or tramp, British informal
a reef is a ridge of rock near the sea surface

explanation.surface: A hiker walking round a rocky outcrop discovers a frog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tramp' is a verb here, to trudge; 'trog' is British slang for walking wearily.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree frog is an amphibian that lives in trees.

clue.text: Ace song employs two pianos put to practical use

indicators.note: employs means the ace and song take the two pianos in among them

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards
a lied is a German art song
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, so two of them make PP

explanation.surface: A top song uses two pianos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piano' is the musical marking for soft, written P.
explanation.definitionFit: Applied, as in applied science, means used in practice rather than theory.

clue.text: Bird with speed making turn to catch bat

indicators.note: to catch means the bat word is held inside the other pieces
making turn means the speed word is turned to read backwards

parts.note: pace means speed
to bat a ball is to hit it

explanation.surface: A bird doubling back at speed to snatch a flying bat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making turn' changes PACE into ECAP; W + ECAP then 'catch' HIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitecap is a name for several birds with white crowns, such as the redstart.

clue.text: Computer programmer ropes in good old chap

indicators.note: ropes in means the programmer takes the good letter inside

parts.note: a coder writes computer code

explanation.surface: A programmer recruits a kindly elderly man.
explanation.definitionFit: A codger is an informal word for an elderly man.

clue.text: One to avoid, Luke at last in contact with his father?

indicators.note: at last means only the final letter of Luke is used

parts.note: Darth Vader is the father of Luke Skywalker in Star Wars

explanation.surface: Luke Skywalker finally meets his father, someone he should avoid.
explanation.definitionFit: An evader is a person who dodges or escapes something.

clue.text: Broken phial outside a site that's ancient in city

indicators.note: outside means the reshuffled phial goes round the other pieces
Broken suggests the phial is smashed and its letters scattered

parts.note: Delphi is the site of the ancient Greek oracle

explanation.surface: A smashed glass phial found around an ancient site within a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken' rearranges PHIAL as PHILA, which goes 'outside' A + DELPHI: PHIL-ADELPHI-A.
explanation.definitionFit: Philadelphia is a major city in Pennsylvania, USA.

clue.text: Denisovich perhaps one person leading way

parts.note: I is the speaker, one person referring to themselves
the van is the vanguard, the part leading the way

explanation.surface: Denisovich might be a lone person leading the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks a definition by example: Denisovich is one Ivan.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan Denisovich is the title character of Solzhenitsyn's novel about a Soviet labour camp.

clue.text: Lightly-cooked part missed in savoury dish

indicators.note: missed means the part is left out of the savoury dish

parts.note: Welsh rarebit, melted cheese on toast, is a savoury dish
a bit is a part

explanation.surface: Part of a savoury dish undercooked and overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: Welsh rarebit is a British dish of seasoned melted cheese on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare describes meat cooked only briefly, still red inside.

clue.text: This has plot penned by a woman

definitions.text: This has plot penned by a woman

parts.words: This has plot penned by a woman
parts.note: a novel has a plot, and this one was written by Mary Ann Evans under the male pen name George Eliot

explanation.surface: Something whose plot was written by a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The point is that the woman wrote as George Eliot, a man's name; 'plot' also hints at a garden bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam Bede is George Eliot's first novel, published in 1859.

clue.text: Equestrian discipline is habit coming with time

parts.note: a habit is a garment, a dress, as a nun's or rider's habit
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A rider's discipline is a habit acquired over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habit' reads as a routine; it is a riding habit, a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressage is the competitive training of a horse in precise movements.
